checks: A generic functional can be chosen injective on both finite base sets. Every path step increases exactly one ordered coordinate, so its output base has strictly increasing functional value. For n=0 there is a one-cell path.

The summed fiber contains the Minkowski sum of the selected compact nonempty fibers. If one has zero volume, translating the other by a point of it gives the required lower bound, while two zero volumes require only nonnegativity.
On one common parity coset the sum has even bases, and halving sends them bijectively to output bases and scales fiber volumes by 2^−d.

On the alternating self-sum path the diagonal yields all original masses and the off-diagonal yields exactly the consecutive root means. Convexity of C and integrality put the midpoint sum inside the measured mixed set.
Original 0de198a47cdc74fc:02 is Lemma 3 and Corollary 4. The frozen proof is the pathwise assertion, distinct from the source’s unrestricted root theorem.

overlap.comparison: The accepted proof uses a monotone traversal for a cardinality estimate and integrates superlevel sets to obtain peak and total-root bounds. It does not give the mass sum along each individual full path or the consecutive-pair parity budget.

readability: The midpoint restriction requires both inputs to use the same parity coset, as stated.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Approved. Monotone path cells give distinct output fibers and hence a valid pathwise lower bound, including zero-volume nonempty fibers.
